questions.question: A student measures the mass of a black powder before adding it to hydrogen peroxide. After the reaction, she filters, dries, and weighs the powder again. If the powder acted as a catalyst, what will she observe?
options: The mass of the powder has decreased because it was consumed to speed up the reaction.
The mass of the powder remains the same, but its chemical properties have permanently changed.
The mass of the powder remains the same, and its chemical identity is unchanged.
The mass of the powder has increased because it bonded with the hydrogen peroxide.

questions.question: In a school lab, manganese dioxide is used to speed up the decomposition of hydrogen peroxide. However, when the same powder is added to a reaction between zinc and hydrochloric acid, the rate of reaction does not change. Why is this?
options: Zinc is too unreactive to be affected by any catalyst.
Catalysts are specific to particular reactions, so manganese dioxide cannot speed up the zinc-acid reaction.
The zinc-acid reaction produces hydrogen gas, which deactivates all catalysts.
Manganese dioxide only works at temperatures above 100 degrees Celsius.

questions.question: Amylase is a protein found in human saliva that breaks down starch into sugars. If amylase is boiled before being mixed with starch, the starch is not broken down. What does this tell us about amylase?
options: Boiling converts amylase from a biological catalyst into a non-biological catalyst.
Amylase is an enzyme whose structure is altered by high heat, stopping it from catalysing the reaction.
Amylase is a non-biological catalyst that only works when cooled down below freezing.
Boiling increases the activation energy of the starch, making it impossible to break down.

questions.question: Metal X is placed into a blue solution of metal Y sulfate. After a few minutes, a reddish-brown solid forms on metal X, and the blue color of the solution begins to fade. Which statement correctly explains this observation?
options: Metal Y is more reactive than metal X and has displaced it from the solution.
Metal X is more reactive than metal Y and has displaced it from its salt solution.
Both metals are of equal reactivity, causing them to form a new alloy in the solution.
Metal X has dissolved, and metal Y has evaporated from the solution.

questions.question: When grey magnesium ribbon is added to a blue solution of copper sulfate, a reaction occurs. Which of the following describes the correct observations and chemical changes for this reaction?
options: The solution turns dark blue, and a grey solid is deposited as copper displaces magnesium.
The solution remains blue, and bubbles of hydrogen gas are the only product.
The blue solution fades to colorless, and a brown solid of copper is formed.
The magnesium ribbon melts, and a green solution of copper sulfate remains unchanged.

questions.question: A scientist wants to determine the relative reactivity of three metals: Lead, Iron, and Silver. Which experimental method would provide the most direct evidence to order these metals in a reactivity series?
options: Measuring the electrical conductivity of each metal in its solid state.
Placing each metal into solutions of the other metals' nitrate salts to observe if displacement occurs.
Heating each metal in a vacuum to see which one melts at the lowest temperature.
Comparing the density of each metal by measuring their mass and volume.

questions.question: Why is a rock containing iron compounds considered an iron "ore" only if the iron can be extracted from it economically?
options: All rocks on Earth contain iron, but only those that are magnetic are called ores.
An ore is defined as a rock containing a high enough concentration of a metal compound to make extraction viable.
An ore must contain pure, uncombined iron metal that can be physically shaken out of the rock.
Rocks are only called ores if they contain metals that are more reactive than carbon.

questions.question: Copper can be extracted from copper oxide by heating it with carbon powder, but aluminium cannot be extracted from aluminium oxide using carbon. What is the reason for this difference?
options: Aluminium is more reactive than carbon, so carbon cannot displace it; copper is less reactive than carbon, so carbon can displace it.
Copper oxide is a gas at room temperature, while aluminium oxide is a liquid.
Carbon is a metal that can only displace other metals that have a higher melting point than itself.
Aluminium oxide does not contain oxygen, so carbon cannot react with it.

questions.question: Copper is widely used to make both electrical wiring and cooking pans. Which pair of physical properties makes copper suitable for both of these specific applications?
options: It is low density and brittle.
It is a good electrical conductor and a good thermal conductor.
It is highly reactive with water and has a dull appearance.
It is an insulator of heat but conducts electricity very well.

questions.question: Clay is a soft, moldable material when wet, but after being fired in a high-temperature kiln, it becomes a hard ceramic vase. Which of the following describes a key property of the finished ceramic vase?
options: It is highly flexible and can be easily bent without breaking.
It is hard but brittle, meaning it will crack or shatter easily under a sharp impact.
It is an excellent electrical conductor that can be used for wiring.
It reverts back to a soft, moldable clay as soon as water is added to it.

questions.question: Polyethene is used to make flexible plastic bags, while poly(tetrafluoroethene) or PTFE is used as a non-stick coating on frying pans. What does this diversity of applications demonstrate about plastics?
options: All plastics have identical properties because they are made of the same chemical element.
Plastics are made of polymers, and different polymer structures result in materials with widely different properties.
Non-stick plastics are natural polymers, while flexible plastics are always metals.
Plastics can easily be converted into ceramics by heating them in a domestic oven.

questions.question: Pure gold is very soft and easily scratched, so jewellers often mix it with small amounts of silver and copper to make 9-carat gold. What type of material is 9-carat gold?
options: A pure elemental metal
A composite material made of polymers
An alloy, which is a mixture of elements containing at least one metal
A ceramic compound formed by heating clay

questions.question: Carbon-fibre reinforced plastic (CFRP) consists of thin carbon fibres embedded within a plastic matrix. Why is CFRP used in high-performance racing cars instead of using plastic or carbon alone?
options: Combining them creates a composite material that is both extremely strong and lightweight, improving on the individual properties.
The plastic chemically reacts with the carbon to create a completely new, pure metal.
It makes the car much heavier, which increases the grip of the tyres on the track.
The carbon fibres melt into the plastic to make a highly flexible ceramic.

questions.question: Which of the following statements best describes the chemical structure and formation of a polymer?
options: It is a giant metallic lattice formed by sharing delocalised electrons.
It consists of small, independent gas molecules that repel each other.
It is made of small molecules called monomers that link together to form very long chains of atoms.
It is a mixture of clay and sand that has been fired at high temperatures.

questions.question: Kevlar is a polymer used in bulletproof vests that does not melt or decompose until it reaches temperatures above 450 degrees Celsius. Why do some polymers like Kevlar have such high melting points?
options: Their polymer chains are very short, allowing them to slide around freely.
They are made of single metal atoms held together by weak electrostatic forces.
Strong forces of attraction exist between their long polymer molecules, making them very hard to separate.
They contain large amounts of water trapped inside their structure which cools them down.

questions.question: A student classifies starch, DNA, and proteins as polymers. Her classmate claims that polymers can only be man-made in factories. Who is correct, and why?
options: The classmate, because all natural substances are classified as ceramics or metals.
The student, because polymers can exist naturally (like starch and proteins) as well as being made synthetically.
Neither, because starch, DNA, and proteins are simple monomers, not polymers.
The student, because synthetic polymers like polyethene are the only true polymers.

questions.question: Pure polyvinyl chloride (PVC) is a rigid, stiff plastic used for water pipes. However, when a substance called a plasticiser is added, PVC becomes flexible enough to make artificial leather. How does the plasticiser achieve this change?
options: It chemically bonds the PVC chains together so tightly that they cannot move.
It gets between the polymer molecules, reducing the attraction between them and allowing them to slide past each other more easily.
It dissolves the polymer chains, turning the plastic into a permanent liquid.
It converts the polymer chains into rigid metal atoms.

questions.question: Vulcanised rubber, which contains sulfur cross-links between the polymer chains, is much harder and less flexible than natural rubber. Why do these cross-links change the properties of the rubber?
options: They allow the polymer chains to slide past each other much more easily.
They chemically bind the polymer chains together, preventing them from moving freely relative to one another.
They break the long polymer chains down into small, volatile monomer gas molecules.
They coat the rubber in a layer of slippery grease that prevents friction.

questions.question: When a piece of magnesium ribbon is dropped into a beaker of dilute hydrochloric acid, rapid bubbling is observed. If the gas produced is collected and tested with a burning splint, it makes a 'squeaky pop'. What are the products of this reaction?
options: Magnesium chloride and oxygen gas
Magnesium chloride and hydrogen gas
Magnesium hydroxide and chlorine gas
Magnesium oxide and carbon dioxide gas

questions.question: When a small piece of sodium metal is added to water, it fizzes rapidly, melts into a ball, and moves across the surface. The resulting solution turns universal indicator purple. Which products are responsible for these observations?
options: Sodium oxide and oxygen gas
Sodium chloride and chlorine gas
Sodium hydroxide (making the solution alkaline) and hydrogen gas (causing the fizzing)
Sodium sulfate and carbon dioxide gas

questions.question: A student adds 1 g of manganese dioxide powder to hydrogen peroxide. It fizzes rapidly. After the reaction stops, the student filters, dries, and weighs the manganese dioxide. Which result and explanation are correct?
options: It weighs 1 g because manganese dioxide acts as a catalyst and is not chemically changed or used up.
It weighs less than 1 g because some manganese dioxide was used up to make oxygen.
It weighs more than 1 g because it absorbed oxygen during the rapid reaction.
It weighs 0 g because it dissolved completely to speed up the chemical reaction.

questions.question: A chemist wants to speed up two different reactions: Reaction A (making ammonia) and Reaction B (making sulfuric acid). She tries using iron powder for both. Iron successfully speeds up Reaction A but has no effect on Reaction B. What does this demonstrate?
options: Iron is only a catalyst when it is dissolved in a solvent.
Catalysts are specific to particular reactions, so iron cannot speed up Reaction B.
Reaction B cannot be sped up by any catalyst because it is too slow.
Iron was chemically changed in Reaction A, so there was none left for Reaction B.

questions.question: Amylase is an enzyme found in human saliva that breaks down starch into sugar. If saliva is boiled before adding it to starch, the starch is not broken down. What is the best explanation for this observation?
options: Boiling destroys the starch molecules so the amylase has nothing to react with.
Amylase is a biological catalyst whose structure is permanently altered by high temperatures, stopping it from working.
Boiling increases the activation energy of the starch breakdown reaction.
Boiling converts amylase into a non-biological catalyst which reacts much more slowly.

questions.question: You have four solutions containing different metal nitrates: W, X, Y, and Z. Metal W can displace X and Y from their nitrate solutions. Metal Z cannot displace any of the other metals. Metal Y can displace X from its nitrate solution. What is the order of reactivity from most reactive to least reactive?
options: W, Y, X, Z
Z, X, Y, W
W, X, Y, Z
Y, W, X, Z

questions.question: When magnesium ribbon is added to a blue solution of copper sulfate, the blue color fades, a brown solid forms, and the mixture gets warm. What are the products of this reaction?
options: Magnesium oxide and copper sulfate
Magnesium sulfate solution and copper
Copper oxide and magnesium sulfate solution
Magnesium copper alloy and sulfur dioxide gas

questions.question: To find out where an unknown metal 'M' fits in the reactivity series, a scientist places pieces of 'M' into solutions of zinc sulfate, copper sulfate, and iron sulfate. 'M' reacts with copper sulfate and iron sulfate, but NOT with zinc sulfate. Where does 'M' lie in the reactivity series?
options: Below copper
Above zinc
Between zinc and iron
Between iron and copper

questions.question: A mining company finds a large deposit of rock containing chalcocite (Cu2S). Why is this rock classified as a copper ore?
options: Because it contains pure copper metal that can be easily scraped off the surface.
Because it is a rock that contains copper in a chemical form from which copper can be profitably extracted.
Because it is a synthetic alloy containing copper and sulfur.
Because it is a ceramic material that becomes hard and brittle when heated.

questions.question: Iron can be extracted from iron oxide by heating it with carbon, but aluminum cannot be extracted from aluminum oxide using carbon. What is the reason for this difference?
options: Carbon is more reactive than iron, but less reactive than aluminum.
Aluminum oxide has a lower melting point than iron oxide.
Carbon acts as a catalyst for iron oxide but not for aluminum oxide.
Iron is a transition metal, whereas aluminum is a poor conductor of electricity.

questions.question: An engineer needs a material to build a lightweight, overhead electrical power line. She needs a material that is a good electrical conductor, can be drawn into thin wires without breaking, and will not snap under tension. Which set of properties of metals is she relying on?
options: Thermal conductivity, high density, and brittleness
Electrical conductivity, ductility, and high tensile strength
Malleability, shininess, and low melting point
Electrical conductivity, low density, and high combustibility

questions.question: A potter shapes soft wet clay into a vase and then heats it in a high-temperature kiln. What happens to the material during this heating process?
options: It melts into a liquid and cools down to form a highly flexible plastic.
It undergoes a chemical change to become a hard, brittle ceramic.
It reacts with carbon to form a shiny, malleable metal alloy.
It turns into a polymer composite with high thermal conductivity.

questions.question: Polystyrene is used to make lightweight, insulating foam cups, while PVC is used to make tough, flexible water pipes. What does this tell us about plastics?
options: All plastics have the exact same properties because they are made of the same atoms.
Plastics are made of polymers, and different types of plastics have very different properties.
Polystyrene is a natural polymer, whereas PVC is a synthetic ceramic.
Adding water to any plastic will change its properties from brittle to flexible.

questions.question: Pure gold is very soft and easily scratched, so jewellers often mix gold with other metals like copper or silver to make 18-carat gold. What type of material is 18-carat gold?
options: A composite
A polymer
An alloy
A ceramic

questions.question: Reinforced concrete is made by pouring concrete around steel rods. The concrete is excellent at resisting crushing forces, while the steel rods are excellent at resisting stretching forces. What type of material is reinforced concrete?
options: An alloy
A composite
A ceramic
A synthetic polymer

questions.question: During a polymerization reaction, thousands of ethene molecules link together. Which statement correctly describes this process?
options: Large polymer molecules are broken down into small, highly reactive monomers.
Small monomer molecules join together to form very long chains of atoms called polymers.
Monomers are mixed with metals to form a highly conductible alloy.
Ethene molecules form cross-links with ceramic particles to make a composite.

questions.question: Poly(ethene) can be made in two forms: LDPE (which melts at 115 degrees Celsius) and HDPE (which melts at 135 degrees Celsius). What explains why some polymers have higher melting points than others?
options: They contain fewer chemical bonds, making them easier to break apart.
Their long-chain molecules are packed closer together, making them harder to separate.
They contain tiny metal particles that conduct heat much faster.
They are natural polymers which are inherently resistant to high temperatures.

questions.question: A student classifies materials into 'synthetic' and 'natural'. She puts wool, DNA, and starch in one group, and nylon, polyester, and polythene in another. Which statement is correct about these materials?
options: Only the second group consists of polymers; the first group are ceramics.
Both groups consist of polymers, showing that polymers can exist naturally or be made synthetically.
The first group consists of alloys, while the second group consists of composites.
Natural polymers cannot be melted, whereas synthetic polymers melt easily.

questions.question: PVC is naturally a hard, rigid plastic used for drainpipes. When certain small molecules are added to PVC during manufacturing, it becomes flexible enough to make garden hoses. What are these added molecules, and how do they work?
options: Cross-links, which bind the polymer chains tightly together.
Plasticisers, which get between polymer molecules and allow them to slide over each other more easily.
Catalysts, which speed up the breakdown of the polymer chains.
Monomers, which turn the polymer back into a liquid state.

questions.question: Vulcanised rubber, used in car tyres, is much harder and less flexible than natural rubber. What structural feature is responsible for this change in properties?
options: The removal of all monomer units from the polymer chains.
The addition of plasticisers that keep the chains separated.
The formation of cross-links between the polymer molecules.
The conversion of the rubber into a metallic alloy.

questions.question: When magnesium ribbon is placed in a test tube containing hydrochloric acid, vigorous fizzing is observed. What gas is being produced, and what is the other product?
options: Chlorine gas and magnesium oxide
Hydrogen gas and magnesium chloride salt
Oxygen gas and magnesium hydride
Carbon dioxide gas and magnesium carbonate

questions.question: A teacher adds a small piece of sodium to a trough of water containing universal indicator. The mixture fizzes violently, the sodium melts into a ball and moves across the water, and the indicator turns purple. What are the products of this reaction?
options: Sodium oxide and oxygen gas
Sodium hydroxide and hydrogen gas
Sodium hydride and oxygen gas
Sodium carbonate and hydrogen gas

questions.question: A student measures the mass of a black powder before adding it to hydrogen peroxide solution. After the rapid bubbling stops, they filter out the powder, dry it, and weigh it again. What should they expect to find if the powder acted as a catalyst?
options: The powder has disappeared because it dissolved and reacted completely.
The mass of the powder remains exactly the same, and its chemical properties are unchanged.
The mass of the powder has doubled because it combined with the liquid.
The mass of the powder is slightly less because some was used up to start the reaction.

questions.question: A student tries to speed up the decomposition of hydrogen peroxide using copper oxide instead of manganese dioxide, but the reaction rate does not increase. Why does this happen?
options: Copper oxide is a liquid, and catalysts must be solids to work.
Catalysts are specific, meaning a substance that speeds up one reaction may not affect another.
Catalysts only work if they are heated to their boiling point first.
Copper oxide is too reactive and completely dissolved instead of acting as a catalyst.

questions.question: Amylase is an enzyme found in human saliva that helps break down starch into sugars. If amylase is boiled at a very high temperature before being mixed with starch, the starch is no longer broken down. What does this demonstrate about enzymes?
options: Enzymes are non-biological catalysts that only work at temperatures above boiling.
Enzymes are living organisms that are killed by boiling.
Enzymes are biological catalysts whose specific structures can be destroyed by high heat.
Enzymes are simple metals that melt when boiled.

questions.question: If a strip of zinc metal is placed into a blue solution of copper sulfate, the solution gradually turns colourless and a reddish-brown solid forms on the zinc. What does this experiment demonstrate?
options: Zinc is less reactive than copper, so it is coated by the copper ions.
Zinc is more reactive than copper and displaces copper from its salt solution.
Copper is more reactive than zinc and displaces zinc from its salt solution.
The sulfate ions are highly reactive and have destroyed the zinc strip.

questions.question: When magnesium ribbon is added to a blue copper sulfate solution, the mixture gets warm, the blue colour fades, and a brown solid forms. Which of the following correctly describes the chemical change occurring?
options: Magnesium reacts with water to form magnesium hydroxide, leaving copper sulfate unchanged.
Magnesium displaces copper to form magnesium sulfate solution and solid copper.
Copper displaces magnesium to form copper sulfate solution and solid magnesium.
Magnesium and copper combine to form a new alloy called magnesium-copper sulfate.

questions.question: You are given three metals (X, Y, and Z) and their respective salt solutions. Metal X displaces Y and Z from their solutions. Metal Z cannot displace Y from its solution. How can these displacement reactions be used to arrange the metals in order of reactivity (most to least reactive)?
options: The reactions confirm the sequence as X, then Y, then Z.
The reactions confirm the sequence as Z, then Y, then X.
The reactions show that Y is the most reactive, followed by X, then Z.
Displacement reactions cannot be used to determine reactivity order.

questions.question: A mining company identifies a large deposit of rock containing hematite (iron oxide). What determines whether this rock can be classified as an iron ore?
options: The rock must be magnetic and spark when struck with steel.
The rock must contain enough iron in a chemical form that makes it economically viable to extract.
The rock must consist of pure, uncombined iron metal that only needs to be melted out.
The rock must be located near an active volcano to ensure high temperatures.

questions.question: Iron can be extracted from iron oxide by heating it with carbon, but magnesium cannot be extracted from magnesium oxide using carbon. What is the reason for this difference?
options: Carbon is more reactive than iron but less reactive than magnesium.
Carbon is less reactive than iron but more reactive than magnesium.
Magnesium oxide is a liquid at room temperature, so carbon cannot mix with it.
Iron oxide is a noble gas compound that decomposes without carbon.

questions.question: A designer is selecting a material to make a new lightweight, high-voltage overhead power cable. Which combination of metallic properties is most important for this specific application?
options: High density, dull appearance, and high melting point.
Good electrical conductivity, high tensile strength, and ductility.
Brittleness, high thermal conductivity, and chemical inertness.
High density, malleability, and low electrical resistance.

questions.question: An artist shapes a vase out of soft, wet clay and leaves it to dry. Why must the clay be fired in a high-temperature kiln before it can be used to hold water?
options: Heating turns the clay into a polymer that can bend without breaking.
Heating causes the soft clay particles to fuse chemically, making the ceramic hard and brittle.
Firing makes the clay highly malleable so it can be reshaped easily if dropped.
Firing turns the clay into a metallic alloy that conducts heat well.

questions.question: Polystyrene is a lightweight, insulating plastic used for food cups, while PVC is a tough, water-resistant plastic used for pipes. What explains why these two materials have such different properties despite both being plastics?
options: Plastics are made from polymers, and different types of polymers result in plastics with very different properties.
Polystyrene contains metal impurities, whereas PVC is a pure ceramic material.
PVC is a natural mineral mined from the earth, while polystyrene is synthetic.
All plastics are identical, but polystyrene is stretched more during manufacturing.

questions.question: Pure gold is very soft and easily scratched, so jewellers typically mix it with silver, copper, or zinc to make 18-carat gold. What type of material is this mixture?
options: A polymer
A ceramic
An alloy
A composite

questions.question: Reinforced concrete is made by pouring concrete around a grid of steel rods. Why is reinforced concrete classified as a composite material?
options: It is a single pure substance made of chemically bonded calcium and iron atoms.
It combines two different materials to create a new material with improved properties, such as better tensile and compressive strength.
It is made entirely of biological polymers that decompose easily.
It is an alloy because it contains steel mixed with liquid cement.

questions.question: Polyethylene is a common plastic used to make plastic bags. How is polyethylene formed at the molecular level?
options: By breaking down long hydrocarbon chains into small, independent gas molecules.
By joining many small molecules called monomers together to form very long chains of atoms.
By mixing metallic atoms with ceramic particles at high pressure.
By dissolving carbon atoms in water to create a liquid crystal.

questions.question: Some polymers, like Kevlar, have extremely high melting points and do not melt easily when heated. What is the molecular explanation for this property?
options: Their monomer units are very small and can easily escape into the air.
Their long polymer chains are held together by strong forces, making the molecules hard to separate.
They contain a high percentage of water molecules that cool the material down.
They are made of metals that have low melting points but high boiling points.

questions.question: A student claims that all polymers are artificial materials created by scientists in laboratories. Which of the following facts best disproves this claim?
options: Plastics can be recycled to make new products.
Natural substances like DNA, starch, and cellulose are polymers that exist in nature.
Synthetic polymers are cheaper to produce than metals.
Glass is a natural polymer made from heated sand.

questions.question: PVC plastic pipes are rigid and hard, but PVC medical tubing is highly flexible and bendable. What substance is added to the polymer during manufacturing to make the tubing flexible?
options: A catalyst, which speeds up the decomposition of the polymer chains.
A plasticiser, which gets between the polymer molecules and allows them to slide over each other more easily.
A cross-linking agent, which binds the polymer chains tightly together.
A ceramic filler, which absorbs impact forces.

questions.question: Some types of rubber become much harder and less flexible after they undergo a process called vulcanisation, which introduces sulfur links between the polymer chains. Why does this process change the properties of the rubber?
options: The sulfur links act as a plasticiser, allowing molecules to slide freely.
The cross-links between polymer molecules restrict their movement, making the material harder and less flexible.
The sulfur dissolves the polymer chains, turning them into a liquid.
The cross-links make the rubber molecules shorter and easier to melt.

questions.question: When a piece of magnesium is placed into a test tube of hydrochloric acid, rapid bubbling is observed. If a burning splint is held near the mouth of the tube, a loud 'squeak' or 'pop' sound is heard. What are the products of this reaction?
options: Magnesium chloride salt and hydrogen gas
Magnesium oxide and chlorine gas
Magnesium hydroxide and oxygen gas
Magnesium carbonate and water vapour

questions.question: Potassium reacts violently with cold water, iron reacts slowly with steam when heated, and gold does not react with water or steam at all. What do these observations demonstrate?
options: Gold is the most reactive metal because it does not change.
The reactivity series shows how vigorously metals react compared to each other, with potassium being more reactive than iron, and iron more reactive than gold.
All metals react with water at the same rate if given enough time.
Potassium is a non-metal because it reacts so rapidly.

questions.question: A student wants to speed up the decomposition of hydrogen peroxide. They add manganese dioxide powder. At the end of the reaction, they filter and dry the manganese dioxide. What will they find?
options: The mass of manganese dioxide is unchanged, and its chemical identity is the same.
The mass of manganese dioxide is reduced because it was used up in the reaction.
The manganese dioxide has turned into manganese sulfate.
The mass of manganese dioxide has increased because oxygen bonded to it.

questions.question: Why can iron be used to catalyse the industrial production of ammonia from nitrogen and hydrogen, but it cannot be used to catalyse the breakdown of hydrogen peroxide as effectively as manganese dioxide?
options: Iron is too reactive as a metal to act as a catalyst in more than one reaction.
Catalysts are specific, meaning different reactions generally require different catalysts to speed them up.
Iron only works as a catalyst when it is in liquid form, whereas manganese dioxide works as a solid.
Hydrogen peroxide is an acid and destroys the iron catalyst before it can act.

questions.question: Amylase is an enzyme found in human saliva that speeds up the breakdown of starch into sugars. What would happen if you heated amylase to 100 degrees Celsius before adding it to a starch solution?
options: The reaction would speed up even further because enzymes work better at higher temperatures.
The reaction would slow down or stop because the enzyme is a biological catalyst that loses its shape and function at high temperatures.
The amylase would turn into a synthetic polymer and catalyse a different reaction instead.
The starch would break down into hydrogen gas and a metal salt instead of sugars.

questions.question: A piece of zinc is placed into a test tube containing copper sulfate solution. After some time, the blue color of the solution fades, and a reddish-brown solid deposits on the zinc. What does this experiment demonstrate?
options: Zinc is more reactive than copper and has displaced it from the sulfate solution.
Copper is more reactive than zinc and has displaced it from the sulfate solution.
Sulfate is highly reactive and has decomposed into sulfur dioxide gas.
Zinc has acted as a catalyst to turn the blue copper ions into red copper atoms.

questions.question: When magnesium ribbon is added to a blue solution of copper sulfate, a reaction occurs. Which of the following correctly describes the products formed in this displacement reaction?
options: Magnesium copper alloy and sulfur dioxide gas.
A colorless solution of magnesium sulfate and solid copper metal.
A blue solution of copper magnesium sulfate and hydrogen gas.
Magnesium oxide solid and copper sulfide solution.

questions.question: A scientist tests four metals (W, X, Y, and Z) by placing each metal into solutions of the other metals' nitrate salts. Metal W displaces X and Y, but not Z. Metal X cannot displace any of the other metals. What is the correct order of these metals in the reactivity series, from most reactive to least reactive?
options: Z, W, Y, X
X, Y, W, Z
Z, W, X, Y
W, Z, Y, X

questions.question: Iron is extracted from its ore, hematite (iron oxide), by heating it with carbon in a blast furnace. Why is this extraction method successful for iron but not for aluminum?
options: Carbon is more reactive than iron but less reactive than aluminum, so it can only displace iron.
Carbon is less reactive than iron, so it allows iron to remain in its metallic state.
Aluminum has a lower melting point than iron, causing it to vaporize in the blast furnace.
Iron oxide is a ceramic material, whereas aluminum oxide is a polymer.

questions.question: Copper is widely used to make electrical wiring in household appliances. Which combination of metallic properties makes copper particularly suitable for this specific purpose?
options: High density, brittle nature, and dull appearance.
Good electrical conductivity and high ductility.
High thermal conductivity and low melting point.
High malleability and extremely low strength.

questions.question: Clay is a soft, moldable substance when wet. However, after being fired in a high-temperature kiln, it becomes a ceramic. How do the physical properties of clay change during this process?
options: It becomes highly flexible and gains excellent electrical conductivity.
It transforms into a low-melting-point polymer that is easily reshaped.
It becomes hard, brittle, and resistant to high temperatures.
It becomes a ductile alloy that can be drawn into thin wires.

questions.question: Pure gold is very soft and easily scratched. To make jewelry, jewellers mix pure gold with other metals like copper or silver to form 18-carat gold. What is this mixture called, and how do its properties compare to pure gold?
options: A composite, which is lighter and has a much lower melting point.
An alloy, which is harder and more durable than pure gold.
A polymer, which is highly flexible and can be stretched easily.
A ceramic, which is brittle and highly resistant to heat.

questions.question: Concrete is made by mixing cement, sand, gravel, and water. When reinforced with steel rods, it becomes reinforced concrete, which can withstand both heavy crushing forces and stretching forces. What class of material is reinforced concrete?
options: A polymer, because it contains repeating organic monomers.
An alloy, because it contains a mixture of different metals.
A composite, because it combines materials to produce improved properties.
A ceramic, because it becomes extremely soft when heated to high temperatures.

questions.question: Polyethene is a common plastic used to make shopping bags. How is the structure of polyethene built up from its starting materials?
options: Small, identical ethene monomers join together chemically to form very long chains of atoms.
Large ceramic molecules are broken down into smaller metallic elements.
Carbon and hydrogen atoms form a mixed giant covalent lattice like diamond.
Alternating layers of metal and plastic are glued together with a biological catalyst.

questions.question: Some polymers, such as thermosetting plastics, do not melt when heated but instead char and burn at very high temperatures. What explains this property?
options: Their molecules are small and can easily slide past each other when heated.
Their polymer molecules are held together by strong forces that make them very hard to separate.
They contain high amounts of water trapped within their crystalline structure.
They are made entirely of metallic bonds that conduct heat away too quickly.

questions.question: Polymers are diverse materials found all around us. Which of the following lists contains only naturally occurring polymers?
options: Polyethene, nylon, and PVC.
Starch, cellulose, and natural rubber.
Polyester, polystyrene, and DNA.
Clay, concrete, and bronze.

questions.question: PVC (polyvinyl chloride) is naturally rigid and brittle, making it ideal for drainpipes. However, when certain small molecules called plasticisers are added, it becomes flexible enough to make artificial leather. How do plasticisers achieve this?
options: They create strong cross-links that lock the polymer chains tightly into position.
They get between the polymer molecules, reducing the attractions and allowing them to slide over each other more easily.
They chemically break down the long polymer chains into individual monomers.
They act as catalysts that speed up the melting of the polymer at room temperature.

questions.question: Vulcanised rubber is used to make car tyres. During vulcanisation, sulfur atoms form cross-links between the long rubber polymer chains. How does this structural change affect the properties of the rubber?
options: It makes the rubber softer, more soluble in water, and easier to melt.
It makes the rubber harder, stronger, and less flexible.
It converts the rubber from a natural polymer into a metallic alloy.
It allows the polymer chains to slide over each other much more easily.

questions.question: A student adds a piece of magnesium ribbon to a test tube containing hydrochloric acid. They observe rapid bubbling. What are the products of this chemical reaction?
options: Magnesium chloride solution and hydrogen gas.
Magnesium hydroxide solution and chlorine gas.
Magnesium oxide solid and water vapor.
Magnesium carbonate and hydrogen gas.

questions.question: A small piece of sodium metal is dropped onto a trough of water. It melts into a ball, fizzes rapidly, and moves across the surface. What products are formed from this reaction?
options: Sodium oxide and steam.
Sodium hydride and oxygen gas.
Sodium hydroxide solution and hydrogen gas.
Sodium chloride and hydrogen gas.

questions.question: The reactivity series lists metals in order of their chemical reactivity. If metal A reacts violently with cold water, metal B reacts slowly with warm acid, and metal C does not react with acid at all, what is the correct arrangement of these metals from least reactive to most reactive?
options: A, B, C
C, B, A
B, C, A
C, A, B

questions.question: Potassium is located near the very top of the reactivity series, while iron is located much lower down. When equal-sized pieces of both metals are added to separate test tubes of dilute hydrochloric acid, what difference in behavior would you expect to observe?
options: Iron will react much more vigorously and produce hydrogen gas faster than potassium.
Potassium will react extremely vigorously and dangerously, while iron will react much more slowly.
Neither metal will react because they are both below hydrogen in the reactivity series.
Potassium will form a metal oxide, while iron will form a metal hydroxide.
